## Re-Review: Comment Resolution
All three previous concerns are fixed in the current source and exercised by the new regressions:
- Terminal deadline checks now run after metadata flush/fsync and before committing COMPLETE/sealed status.
- A failed raw-capture inventory scan leaves unsealed evidence, propagates the error, and restores affinity.
- Replay binds each regenerated report digest to its artifact entry and saved bytes.

I attempted to resolve the three addressed threads, but GitHub denied ResolveReviewThread permission for this reviewer account. Please resolve them; they are not remaining code blockers.

## Review Summary
Reviewed the three-file follow-up (168 additions, 42 deletions) across bug detection, error handling, test coverage, comment accuracy, and guideline/approval-contract compliance. One introduced handoff blocker remains, described inline: the candidate protocol and review package still bind the old runner and regression-test hashes. The actual pinned-helper checks reject both current files, and approval permits no later helper-pin change.

## Verification
- All 68 inquiry Python tests passed, including complete-run deadline expiration with persistent recovery failure, persistent stdout EIO, and all report-inventory mutation/schema cases.
- Real wall-clock deadline probe delayed metadata fsync past its deadline; publication raised AggregateDeadline, left the previous checkpoint byte-identical, and replay refused the unsealed checkpoint.
- Real legacy replay CLI preserved all 567 retained files byte-for-byte and the expected INCOMPLETE result.
- Real CLI rejected a checksum-valid archive with summary.json omitted from its inventory before creating the destination.
- Both 96-case authoring checks, the 80-case finite audit, and ARA source-span/session-index/observation gates passed.
- Direct execution of the same checked() calls used by repository_preflight rejected the current runner and test against the candidate’s stale hashes.

The earlier full local-gates run passed at 26ba9c4. This follow-up changes only Python, tests, and documentation, so Lean/Haskell gates were not repeated. No production inquiry drivers or fresh P8 measurement were invoked.

## Positive Observations
The fixes fail closed at persisted-evidence boundaries, and the new tests assert retained state, affinity restoration, and refusal before destination creation rather than implementation wiring. Original evidence and pending measurement approval remain untouched.
